items.question: What is a constructor in Java?
items.answer: Answer: A constructor is a special member of a class used to initialize objects. It has the same name as the class and no return type. It is called when an object is created using new.

What is constructor chaining?
items.answer: Answer: Constructor chaining is the process of calling one constructor from another constructor. It helps reuse initialization code and avoid duplication. The two types covered in the lecture are: Super constructor chaining — using super(...) to call a parent-class constructor. Local constructor chaining — using this(...) to call another constructor in the same class.

What is encapsulation in Java?
items.answer: Answer: Encapsulation is the process of binding data members and member functions together and controlling access to the data. It is commonly achieved by making fields private and providing public getters and setters.
